indicators.healthyLifeExpectancyHale: WHO WHOSIS_000002 (HALE at birth, both sexes)
indicators.warDeaths: UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset 26.1: state-based and one-sided violence

sourcePolicy.worldBank: World Bank supplies life expectancy, GNI per capita (PPP), GDP per capita (PPP) only to extend GNI to years without it (or, before a country's first GNI year, in its place), intentional homicides/100k, road traffic deaths/100k (WHO estimates), population, and country/group metadata.
sourcePolicy.ucdp: War deaths come from the UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset (state-based conflict and one-sided violence against civilians). Each death counts for the country whose people died: a government's soldiers for that government's country (the first listed, for a coalition), and armed groups, civilians and unidentified dead for the country where they died, with Gaza and the West Bank counted as Palestine.
sourcePolicy.whoGho: HALE is the only WHO GHO input: WHOSIS_000002, healthy life expectancy at birth, both sexes. Missing annual HALE values are estimated by preserving the latest reported life-expectancy-minus-HALE gap, keeping its sign, and applying it to current life expectancy.
sourcePolicy.humanFreedomIndex: Freedom is derived from the Cato Institute and Fraser Institute Human Freedom Index 2025 Personal Freedom categories, excluding Security and Safety to keep it distinct from the tracker’s Safety pillar.

derivedRows: Derived rows are population-weighted aggregates computed from the country rows in this file using World Bank data for abundance, homicide and road deaths, life expectancy, and population; UCDP for war deaths; WHO GHO for HALE; and the Human Freedom Index for personal freedom. GNI per capita (PPP) is used for abundance; a year without GNI moves the latest GNI by the change in GDP per capita (PPP) since then, and plain GDP per capita stands in only before a country's first GNI year.
healthPillar: LEI = ½·LEI(life expectancy) + ½·LEI(HALE); both score 0 at 20 years and 1 at 85 years, and keep rising past 85. A World Bank life expectancy more than 5 years below the latest WHO HALE on or before its year is treated as a source error and dropped (sourceRefresh.lifeExpectancyCheck lists them); that year uses the latest earlier value.
safetyNote: Safety scores intentional homicides per 100k as 1 / (1 + homicides / 100): 0 scores 1, 100 scores 0.5, 200 scores 1/3, and no number scores 0. War deaths (UCDP state-based and one-sided violence, counted for the country whose people died and divided by its population; years with none recorded count as 0) and road deaths per 100k are published alongside for context but are not part of the index, and a country-year doesn't need them to be scored. Suicide, other accidents, and non-fatal crime are not included.
freedomNote: Freedom averages the Personal Freedom categories for rule of law, movement, religion, association, expression, and relationships from the Cato/Fraser Human Freedom Index 2025, then rescales the result from 0-10 to 0-100. The Security and Safety category is excluded to keep the pillar distinct from Safety.
pillarNormalization: Every base pillar is normalized against fixed goalposts, and the index is 1 + the natural log of the pillars' weighted geometric mean: 1 + Σ weight·ln(pillar). 1 means every goalpost is met. Scores are absolute and do not depend on other countries or the selected year. The ranking is the geometric mean's, so weakness in one pillar drags the index down, and every halving of a pillar costs its weight × ln 2 however low it already is, so the index has no floor. Health (above 85 years) and abundance (above $75,000) keep rising past 1, so it has no ceiling either.

globalAverageSeries.definition: Comparable fixed-cohort trend: the same 94 countries are included in every year from 2000-2025, weighted by their population in each year. This avoids false jumps when countries enter the dataset. It covers 3627 million people in 2000 and 4661 million in 2025; it is not a whole-world estimate.
globalAverageSeries.footNote: 2000 0.7394 → 2025 0.7755. Fixed cohort of 94 countries present in every year; population-weighted within that cohort. Coverage grows from 3627M to 4661M people.
